page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 16 virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 hyperthreads per core. CPU allocation is fully dedicated, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache. The instance features instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512 foundation, AES cryptography, FMA, BMI2, and ADX.

Provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual core. It does not include dedicated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled by default.

Benchmark data reveals average multi-core processing and high-concurrency throughput alongside weaker single-threaded execution. Synthetic CPU testing via multi-core stress-ng reached 11,776.53, and the Geekbench multi-core test scored 5,757.0, both placing in the average benchmark tier. Conversely, single-threaded execution showed lower performance, with single-core stress-ng scoring 1,108.98 and single-core Geekbench scoring 893.0. In memory throughput testing, uncached large-block reads registered at 75.3 GB/sec and uncached writes at 53.85 GB/sec.

Application-level benchmarks demonstrate strong suitability for in-memory data structures and web serving. The server achieved 11.19 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 7.73 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model, it recorded 861.69 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 142.38 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers strong resource density for RAM-bound applications that do not demand top-tier single-thread CPU performance. Due to its dedicated 128 GB memory footprint, lack of local storage overhead, and average multi-threaded capacity, it is well suited for enterprise database nodes, Redis caching layers, medium-scale web application backends, and data transformation pipelines.
